full_text_en:
Linqing City Automobile Repair Factory v. Beijing Youth Economic Development Corporation

— Dispute over Technology Transfer Contract

Plaintiff (Transferee): Shandong Province Linqing City Automobile Repair Factory (hereinafter referred to as the Repair Factory).

Legal Representative: Hao Yiling, Factory Director of the Repair Factory.

Agents ad litem: Zhang Fengxiang, Deputy Factory Director of the Repair Factory; Shi Qichao, Attorney at the Dongcheng District Legal Advisory Office, Beijing.

Defendant (Transferor): Beijing Youth Economic Development Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Development Corporation).

Legal Representative: Sha Wanquan, Chairman of the Board of the Development Corporation.

Agents ad litem: Zhang Qizhen, Manager of the Science and Technology Development Department of the Development Corporation; Chen Jinzhan, Attorney at the Chongwen District Legal Advisory Office, Beijing.

On April 23, 1985, the Plaintiff Repair Factory and the Defendant Development Corporation entered into a technology transfer contract for the "Vertical Vibratory Finishing Machine." The contract provided that: the Development Corporation would provide all technical drawings and materials to the Repair Factory, and dispatch technical personnel to conduct personnel training and prototype debugging at the Repair Factory; the Repair Factory would pay the Development Corporation a technology transfer fee of RMB 12,000; if the Repair Factory failed in debugging and could not meet the design requirements, the Development Corporation would refund the full technology transfer fee; from the effective date of the contract, if either party breached the contract, the breaching party would be liable for a daily penalty of 0.1% of the transfer fee. The contract also contained provisions regarding profit sharing, trademark use, compensation for technical personnel, and the obligation of both parties not to disseminate the technology to any third party.

After the contract was signed, the Repair Factory paid the Development Corporation the technology transfer fee of RMB 12,000, collected all the technical drawings, and proceeded to manufacture the prototype according to the drawings. During the production process, the Repair Factory discovered numerous errors in the drawings, and the prototype produced based on the drawings was unusable. Consequently, the Repair Factory sent personnel to negotiate with the Development Corporation on several occasions to resolve the errors in the drawings, but the parties failed to reach an agreement. In January 1986, the Repair Factory filed a lawsuit with the Dongcheng District People's Court of Beijing, requesting the court to adjudicate the termination of the contract; order the Development Corporation to refund the full technology transfer fee and pay a daily penalty of 0.1% of the transfer fee as stipulated in the contract; and compensate for the economic losses incurred from the scrapped products due to the errors in the drawings. The Defendant Development Corporation argued that the reason the contract could not be performed on time was that the Plaintiff lacked processing capacity and had commenced production without following the standard production procedures for mechanical products, thereby preventing the Development Corporation from carrying out the subsequent work.

After accepting the case, the Dongcheng District People's Court commissioned the China Technology Market Development Center to conduct a technical appraisal and on-site investigation of the subject matter of the "Vertical Vibratory Finishing Machine" technology transfer contract. The appraisal report stated: "There are a large number of errors in the working blueprints; the drawings are disorganized, with incomplete annotations and no signatures of technical personnel. These drawings do not comply with the relevant national standards and cannot be used for production." "Among the 68 technical drawings, 22 contain major errors." "Some working blueprints have incomplete dimensional annotations, rendering it impossible to cut materials or conduct inspections." The parts manufactured by the Repair Factory were verified to meet the requirements of the Development Corporation's drawings. Due to fundamental design errors, the equipment assembled from the processed parts was completely scrapped, resulting in losses of RMB 11,101.28. The Dongcheng District People's Court, in accordance with Article 26, Paragraph 2 of the Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and the technical appraisal report provided by the China Technology Market Development Center, held that the technology transfer contract originally signed by the Repair Factory and the Development Corporation was valid; the primary reason for the contract's non-performance was that the technical drawings provided by the Defendant contained numerous errors and could not be used for actual production. The Defendant was the party responsible for the dispute.

Having ascertained the facts and clarified the responsibilities, the Dongcheng District People's Court, in accordance with Article 97 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), presided over mediation between the parties. The Defendant Development Corporation acknowledged that it had caused economic losses to the other party by transferring immature technology and expressed willingness to compensate. The Plaintiff also made appropriate concessions, reducing the amount of damages claimed and waiving its request for the Defendant to pay liquidated damages. Both the Plaintiff and the Defendant voluntarily reached the following agreement: 1. The technology transfer contract for the "Vertical Vibratory Finishing Machine" signed by the parties on April 23, 1985, shall be terminated. 2. The Defendant shall refund to the Plaintiff the technology transfer fee of RMB 12,000 and pay the Plaintiff damages of RMB 9,000. 3. The Plaintiff shall return to the Defendant the technical drawings and materials for the "Vertical Vibratory Finishing Machine" and deliver to the Defendant the materials used in manufacturing the prototype. 4. The Plaintiff shall not further use the technology provided by the Defendant to produce finishing machines or disseminate such technology to others.
